## Paper

Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

On-policy actor-critic / PPO.

## Theoretical benchmark

No economic-theory benchmark. The paper's method benchmark is empirical comparison against other online policy-gradient methods on standard RL tasks.

## Learning setup

PPO alternates on-policy rollout collection with multiple minibatch epochs on a clipped surrogate policy objective. The relevant implementation ingredients are old-policy probability ratios, clipped updates, advantage estimates, value-function learning, and entropy regularization.

## Metrics

Paper-side: average episodic return/learning curves, sample complexity, simplicity, and wall-time on benchmark RL tasks. Repo-side: task metrics from the artificial-economies worlds plus finite-run validation outputs.

## Main result

PPO outperforms other online policy gradient methods and strikes a favorable balance between sample complexity, simplicity, and wall-time.

## What we need to reproduce

Do not reproduce Atari/MuJoCo for this thesis. Reproduce the method-level obligation: PPO must be an on-policy actor-critic baseline with clipped surrogate updates, advantage estimation, value loss, entropy bonus, and repeated minibatch epochs, then compare it against DQN/Q-learning/MARL inside the artificial-economies worlds.

## How our project differs

The paper validates PPO as a general RL algorithm on standard control/game benchmarks. This repo adapts PPO to structured observations and discrete economic actions, then asks whether its learned economic behavior differs from tabular Q-learning, DQN, independent-DQN, and centralized-critic agents.

## Implementation obligations

Categorical discrete policy; separate value function; stored old log probabilities; GAE-style advantage computation; clipped probability-ratio surrogate; value loss; entropy bonus; minibatch epochs over on-policy rollout batches.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Check minds/deep_rl/torch_ppo_mind.py for the PPO update structure; test_phase3_deep_rl.py for PPO integration/validation; outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv and cross-world mind-comparison tables for behavior.

## Failure modes to audit

PPO label without clipped old-policy ratio; stale/off-policy replay used as if PPO; missing value baseline or advantage estimates; no entropy/value terms; only smoke tests without full-run comparison against DQN/Q-learning.

## Project code comparison

minds/deep_rl/torch_ppo_mind.py implements a structured-observation discrete PPO mind with Categorical actions, policy/value networks, rollout storage, GAE parameters, clipped surrogate objective, value loss, entropy coefficient, and minibatch epochs. That satisfies the method-level obligation for this thesis, but it does not reproduce the original paper's continuous-control, Atari, sample-complexity, or wall-time benchmark suite. The thesis-valid comparison is therefore PPO versus Q-learning/DQN/MARL on the economic-world outputs, not PPO versus TRPO/A2C on Atari/MuJoCo.
